newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia bank Celje buys into bank Hmezad.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia bank Celje buys into bank Hmezad.

text.p: Slovenia's fifth largest bank Banka Celje said on Tuesday it had increased its stake in rival Hmezad to 40 percent from 15 percent and announced plans for cooperation in some business areas.

"We recently bought Hmezad shares in the value of 600 million tolars ($4.0 million) to take our stake in Hmezad to 40 percent in order to achieve synergies," Celje chief executive Niko Kac told Reuters.
He said the deal had already been approved by the Bank of Slovenia and by shareholders of both banks.

"The two banks will remain independent but will join some of their services. Thus we will perform foreign financial transactions for clients of bank Hmezad, issue common credit cards and have a unified information technology," Kac said.

The move follows Celje's January 1 take-over of competitor Noricum with balance sheet assets of 6.5 billion tolars ($43.6 million). Celje has said it aims to increase its market share to 5.7 percent by 1998 from 3.8 percent.
Analysts have forecast a wave of Slovenian banking mergers in the next few years as the sector tries to reduce costs and gears up for foreign competition.
There are currently 28 banks operating in Slovenia but parliament is expected to pass a law later this year enabling foreign banks to establish branches in Slovenia.

Kac said Banka Celje expected to have a net profit of one billion tolars ($6.7 million) in 1996, up from 800 million in 1995. Assets rose 30 percent to 90.3 billion tolars over the same period and should jump another 25 percent this year.
Bank Hmezad's total assets rose 25 percent to 10.3 billion tolars last year.
Kac said Celje planned to apply for a listing on the Ljubljana bourse in 1998 once a law governing acquisitions of 25 percent or more was in place. The law has been in preparation for two years.
"We would like to wait for the take-over law to be introduced before applying for a listing," Kac explained.
